'Just a tidy number on a form': the form rises big and centre while Lustig stands small and composed at the edge; strong push makes the paper outweigh the man

b75.caption: So what was the sentence?
b75.why: 'So what was the sentence?': back at the tower where it began, Lustig walks in and raises one finger - the key point is coming; a still hold leaves the question hanging

b76.why: 'Give people a reason to feel special, and they will help you fool them': Lustig's open-palm offer, the mark grinning over his own cash; pan carries us from the flattery to the payment

'help you fool them': under the lit tower Lustig steps toward us with his hand out, inviting the handshake that makes the mark his helper; pull widens so the offer sits small against the tower he sold

b77.why: 'The tower never moved': slow pan right onto the real tower standing exactly where it always was, a Parisian reads the old scandal in the paper at left
'The man who sold it only borrowed a little of our oldest weakness': Lustig stands at the foot of the tower with an innocent shrug - only borrowed; camera pulls wide so the tower outlasts him

b78.why: 'If this story surprised you': Lustig strides back into the sunset plaza where the hook began and turns his finger on the viewer; push in, coin flips up - we are the next mark

'tell me which part of the con you would have fallen for': Lustig walks out of the hotel door heading left, open palm pitching again, and a tiny tower rises between him and a doubtful chin-in-hand mark; pan left follows his walk - the comments are his next pitch

needed_plates.desc: 1920s Chicago street at night, hand-drawn ink and watercolour style matching the Paris plates: brick buildings with fire escapes, neon-less painted speakeasy sign, a parked black 1920s sedan at far right (x 80-100%), lamp posts at x ~12% and ~88%, wet asphalt from y ~63% down fully open, centre x 20-80% clear for two actors

Exterior of a 1930s New York federal detention building at night, same ink style: tall grey stone wall with barred windows, one window at upper-left open with a knotted white bedsheet rope hanging down to the street, searchlight beam across a navy sky, sidewalk from y ~63% down open, centre and right clear for a sneaking actor

Alcatraz island prison seen from the shore/dock in heavy grey fog, same ink style: cellhouse and lighthouse on the rock at right (x 60-95%), choppy grey bay water mid-ground, wooden dock planks foreground from y ~65% down fully open, left/centre clear for one actor; mood bleak and lonely

Palatial hotel salon interior: gilded panelled walls, two crystal chandeliers, tall mirrors, red velvet chairs pushed to the edges, polished parquet floor open y 66-100% full width, centre clear for 2-3 standing figures

1889 Paris World's Fair (Exposition Universelle) on the Champ de Mars, sunny day: the brand-new Eiffel Tower, painted red-brown, at right (x 68-95%), flags and bunting, exhibition pavilions and small crowds in the distance; open sandy foreground from y ~65% down, centre-left clear for actors. Same hand-drawn ink and watercolour style as the existing plates, 16:9.

Montmartre-style Paris cafe terrace by day: small round marble tables with chairs, striped awning, easels and canvases leaning on the wall at left, the Eiffel Tower small and dark on the far skyline at right; open paved floor from y ~65% down, a table at centre-left (x 35-45%) for a petition prop. Same ink and watercolour style, 16:9.

Foot of the Eiffel Tower around 1910: a wooden military radio hut with antenna wires running up into the tower legs at right (x 65-100%), a tricolour flag, sandbags; overcast sky; open ground from y ~65% down, centre-left clear for a soldier actor. Same ink and watercolour style, 16:9.

Close view of the Eiffel Tower's lower ironwork in grey weather: rusted, flaking red-brown girders and rivets filling the right half, paint peeling, a painter's ladder and paint buckets on scaffolding; open ground band from y ~66% down at left and centre for one actor. Same ink and watercolour style, 16:9.

1920s French government office interior by day: dark wooden desk with stacks of papers and ledgers at right-centre, tall window with the Eiffel Tower faintly visible, filing cabinets, framed tricolour seal on the wall; open wooden floor from y ~68% down, centre-left clear for an actor. Same ink and watercolour style, 16:9.

Small Bohemian country town c.1890: cobbled square, pastel gabled houses with red tile roofs, onion-dome church tower at left, chestnut trees, overcast morning; hand-drawn ink + flat colour matching the Paris plates; open cobbled foreground from y ~65% down, centre x 25-80% clear for actors, no Eiffel Tower

1920s European police records office interior: wooden filing cabinets and pigeonholes stacked with folders at left and right, desk lamp, map of Europe pinned on back wall with string between cities, dim lamplight; open wooden floor from y ~66% down, centre clear for one or two actors

First-class promenade deck of a 1920s transatlantic ocean liner by day: white railing at y ~58%, open sea and horizon behind, lifeboats and a funnel at top right, wooden deck chairs at far left; teak deck floor from y ~64% down fully open, centre x 20-80% clear for actors

1920s first-class ocean liner stateroom at night: round porthole with moonlit sea at centre-left, brass lamp, writing desk with inkwell and papers at left (x 5-25%), wood panelling, steamer trunk at right; open carpet floor from y ~66% down

Paris tailor's fitting room 1925: tall gilt mirror at right-centre, rack of dark formal tailcoats and top hats at left, bolts of cloth on shelves, warm afternoon light; open wooden floor from y ~66% down, centre-left clear for an actor

Cramped dim room at night, wooden desk under a green banker's lamp, inkwell, rubber stamps, stacks of blank letterhead with a French tricolour government crest, wastebasket of crumpled drafts; empty floor y 68-100% left-centre for a standing figure, desk right half

Hotel de Crillon neoclassical colonnaded facade on Place de la Concorde, daytime warm light, obelisk at left edge, grand arched entrance right-centre with doorman post, wide open cobbled/paved foreground y 64-100%
1920s Paris scrap-metal yard by day: heaps of rusty girders, wheels and pipes left and right, a small office shed with sign 'Ferraille', overcast sky, open dirt ground y 64-100% centre clear

Grand Paris club dining room at night, 1925: long banquet table seen side-on across the right half (x 45-100%, tabletop y ~62%), candelabras and silverware, tall-backed chairs all occupied by silhouetted gentlemen except ONE empty chair with a glowing place setting at x ~68%; chandelier above, dark panelled walls; open floor on the left half y 66-100% for two standing actors; same ink-and-watercolour style, 1672x941

Paris boulevard outside the Hotel de Crillon, 1925, grey-bright afternoon: two long black 1920s limousines with chauffeurs parked right-centre (x 50-95%, wheels at y ~70%), stone hotel facade with flags behind, plane trees; open cobbled pavement y 66-100% on the left half for actors; same ink-and-watercolour style and framing as paris_dusk, 1672x941

Modest bourgeois Paris parlour at night, 1925: patterned wallpaper, small fireplace with a clock at centre-left, armchair at far left, oil lamp glowing on a side table at far right (x ~90%), heavy curtains; plain wooden floor y 66-100% open across the centre for a husband and wife standing; same ink-and-watercolour style, 1672x941

Paris Gare de l'Est interior at night, hand-drawn ink and watercolour matching existing plates: iron-and-glass arched roof, steam locomotive with carriages along the right third (x 65-100%), warm gas lamps, platform clock top-centre, open stone platform floor from y ~65% to bottom across full width, centre-left clear for actors.

Vienna Ringstrasse street at dusk, 1925, same ink-and-watercolour style: Baroque facades and a church spire (Stephansdom-like) right-centre, tram wires, orange-pink sky, gas lamps at x ~12% and ~88%, open cobbled foreground from y ~63% down, centre clear for one or two actors. No Eiffel Tower.

Viennese coffee-house interior in morning light, 1925: marble tables, bentwood chairs, newspaper rack on wooden holders at left (x 0-15%), tall windows onto a Vienna street at right, warm cream walls, open wooden floor from y ~66% down, centre clear for a standing actor.

Exterior of a 1920s Paris commissariat at grey daytime: stone facade with blue-white-red flag and 'POLICE' lamp over a dark double door at right (x 75-92%), wet cobbles from y ~63% down, centre-left open for two actors facing each other.

Hand-drawn ink-and-wash 1930s New York street at night, 16:9: brick tenements and a lit pawnshop/bank front on the right third, fire escapes, wet asphalt reflecting yellow streetlamps, a parked black 1930s sedan far right; open empty pavement foreground y 62-100% across x 15-80% for stick figures standing feet ~y 83%; no people, no text.

Dim 1920s American back room / hotel suite workroom: single green-shaded hanging lamp, wooden workbench at right with tools and a small mahogany box with brass crank, venetian blinds, wallpaper; wooden floor y 66-100% open, actors left and centre

Dusty 1920s small Texas town main street, bright day, false-front wooden storefronts, a sheriff's office sign right, water tower and a parked Model-T, tumbleweed; sandy ground y 64-100% open across full width

Al Capone's 1920s Chicago hotel office (Lexington Hotel): dark wood panelling, big mahogany desk right of centre (x 60-85%) with ashtray and phone, leather chair, framed portrait, window with blinds and city lights; wooden floor y 66-100% open, actors left and centre
1920s American bank vault: wall of brass safe-deposit boxes left-to-right, massive round steel vault door open at right (x 70-95%), marble floor y 66-100% open, actors left and centre

Hand-drawn ink-and-wash 1930s jail cell interior, 16:9: grey stone walls, iron-barred door on left (x 0-20%), high barred window at right (x 65-85%, y 15-40%) with moonlight shaft, narrow cot with white bedsheet at back wall, open stone floor y 65-100% centre clear for one actor; cold blue-grey palette; no people, no text.

Hand-drawn ink-and-wash view of Alcatraz island prison in 1930s, 16:9: the rocky island with cellhouse and lighthouse on the right half under heavy grey fog, choppy grey-green bay, a wooden dock in the foreground spanning x 0-70% with open planks y 64-100% for actors; bleak, cold; no people, no text.

Hand-drawn ink-and-wash 1940s prison hospital ward, 16:9: pale green tiled walls, row of white iron beds receding left, one bed in centre-left foreground (x 30-60%) sized for a stick figure propped up, small barred window with dim afternoon light at right, bedside cabinet right-centre; quiet, sad; no people, no text.

Hand-drawn ink-and-wash 1940s county records office, 16:9: dark wooden counter/desk across left-centre (x 15-65%, top at y ~70%) with an ink stamp and pen, tall filing cabinets and wall clock behind, green banker's lamp; open floor right (x 60-90%) for a clerk; muted brown palette; no people, no text.

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black flat cap) climbing down a knotted bedsheet rope, both hands gripping the rope, legs wrapped, sly grin looking back over shoulder; facing right; full body on flat magenta background

Victor Lustig in black-and-white striped prison uniform and no cap, shoulders slumped, head bowed, hands cuffed in front, sad downturned mouth and drooping eyebrows; standing front-on; full body on flat magenta background
Victor Lustig dressed as a French ministry official: black tailcoat, top hat, white gloves, tricolour sash, holding a leather briefcase, chin up, solemn official expression, facing right

Parisian bystander (brown flat cap, brown herringbone tweed jacket, bright orange scarf, dark brown trousers), front-on, head tipped back looking up and to the right, mouth open in wonder, one hand holding the cap on his head. Same stick style: white round head, long black stick legs.
City official stickman in a black bowler hat, grey frock coat and waistcoat, facing right, holding a rolled document with a red wax seal at chest height, stern neutral face.

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black beret), front-on, holding an open newspaper low enough to show his face, eyes narrowed with a slow sly smile, one eyebrow raised.

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black beret) leaning forward facing right, fountain pen in right hand reaching down as if writing the last word on something just in front of him at waist height (the newspaper is a separate prop), sly half-smile, full body, same stick style.

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black flat cap), three-quarter right, tipping his cap with one gloved hand, other hand open in greeting, mouth mid-word, warm charming smile; five small speech bubbles fan out above his head, each holding a tiny flag (France, Germany, Bohemia/Czech, Italy, Britain) instead of text

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black flat cap), leaning forward toward the right, one hand half-raised beside his mouth as if murmuring a quiet word to someone close, calm half-closed eyes, soft half-smile; NOT a finger on the lips

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black flat cap), three-quarter right, leaning slightly forward with chin resting lightly on his knuckles, eyes wide and fixed on an unseen speaker, eyebrows up, small attentive smile: utterly absorbed listener

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black flat cap), front-on, holding a fan of five small dark passports in one gloved hand like playing cards, sly smirk, other hand on hip

Same 1920s European police inspector (dark uniform with brass buttons, kepi cap, moustache), front-on, holding two open manila file folders side by side, one in each hand, eyes darting between them, baffled frown, small sweat drop
Wealthy 1920s passenger stick figure (white linen suit, straw boater, cigar, gold watch chain), relaxed open-mouthed chatting pose, one hand gesturing, facing right
Victor Lustig in profile facing right, hunched forward writing with a fountain pen on a sheet held in the other hand, concentrated narrowed eyes, small sly smile
Middle-aged businessman stick figure (brown suit, bowler hat, round spectacles), facing right, mid-sentence with mouth open and both hands gesturing expansively, pleased with himself
Victor Lustig, three-quarter right, head tilted in an agreeable nod, one hand on heart and the other open palm forward, warm sympathetic smile
Loud flashy stick figure (checked suit, red tie, cigar), front-on, mouth wide open shouting, one arm flung up, motion lines around head
Victor Lustig facing right, stepping forward with right hand extended for a handshake, friendly warm smile, other hand tipping his cap

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black beret) standing, leaning over, pen in right hand writing on a sheet held flat in left, sly concentrated smirk, facing right
Hotel doorman stick figure in burgundy long coat with gold buttons and braid, peaked cap, white gloves, bowing politely with one hand on chest, facing right
Scrap-metal dealer stick figure, stocky, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache, rubbing hands together with hungry wide eyes and grin, facing front

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), front-on, shoulders slumped, face red, eyes down, hat in limp hand: publicly shamed.

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), front-on, hand on chin, one eyebrow raised, frown: doubt creeping in.

Victor Lustig without beret, in grey-and-white striped prison uniform, standing slumped front-on, arms hanging, head tilted down, sad droopy eyes, small frown; same white round head and stick limbs as the cast.

Victor Lustig (cast style, beret, navy coat, scarf, orange pocket square) standing front-on, one arm extended pointing straight at the camera/viewer, other hand on hip, knowing sly grin with one raised eyebrow.
